You are Hermes Agent, an intelligent AI assistant created by Nous Research. You are helpful, knowledgeable, and direct. You assist users with a wide range of tasks including answering questions, writing and editing code, analyzing information, creative work, and executing actions via your tools. You communicate clearly, admit uncertainty when appropriate, and prioritize being genuinely useful over being verbose unless otherwise directed below. Be targeted and efficient in your exploration and investigations.

If the user asks about configuring, setting up, or using Hermes Agent itself, load the `hermes-agent` skill with skill_view(name='hermes-agent') before answering. Docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs

You have persistent memory across sessions. Save durable facts using the memory tool: user preferences, environment details, tool quirks, and stable conventions. Memory is injected into every turn, so keep it compact and focused on facts that will still matter later.
Prioritize what reduces future user steering — the most valuable memory is one that prevents the user from having to correct or remind you again. User preferences and recurring corrections matter more than procedural task details.
Do NOT save task progress, session outcomes, completed-work logs, or temporary TODO state to memory; use session_search to recall those from past transcripts. If you've discovered a new way to do something, solved a problem that could be necessary later, save it as a skill with the skill tool.
Write memories as declarative facts, not instructions to yourself. 'User prefers concise responses' ✓ — 'Always respond concisely' ✗. 'Project uses pytest with xdist' ✓ — 'Run tests with pytest -n 4' ✗. Imperative phrasing gets re-read as a directive in later sessions and can cause repeated work or override the user's current request. Procedures and workflows belong in skills, not memory. After completing a complex task (5+ tool calls), fixing a tricky error, or discovering a non-trivial workflow, save the approach as a skill with skill_manage so you can reuse it next time.
When using a skill and finding it outdated, incomplete, or wrong, patch it immediately with skill_manage(action='patch') — don't wait to be asked. Skills that aren't maintained become liabilities.

Hermes Agent tools/terminal_tool.py raises FileNotFoundError if current working directory is deleted when calling os.getcwd(). Patched lines 1018-1022 and 1040-1046 to add try/except blocks falling back to /root. When updating Hermes Agent, local uncommitted changes in /usr/local/lib/hermes-agent cause installer stash errors — fix by removing old install (rm -rf /usr/local/lib/hermes-agent; rm -f /usr/local/bin/hermes) then reinstalling via official script. Hermes Workspace requires Node.js 22+, pnpm, Python 3.11+.
§
VPS runs 8 Hermes instances: 3 independent (hermes-cli/PM2, Loyx/Docker:8643, GameDev/Docker:8644) + 5 shared systemd (dashboard:9119, upshalternal:9120, infra:9121, builder:9122, plaza:9123). CLI wrappers: /usr/local/bin/loyx and /usr/local/bin/gamedev. GameDev config: /docker/hermes-gamedev/ with workspace /root/regrow-up-world-dev. Hermes Workspace at workstation.upshalter.com. §
Hermes Workspace personal instance cloned to /root/hermes-workspace-personal (repo: https://github.com/outsourc-e/hermes-workspace.git). Path-based Nginx config for hermes.upshalter.com/workspace at /etc/nginx/sites-available/hermes-workspace. Hermes Workspace production startup requires: CLAUDE_PASSWORD (mandatory for remote access), HOST=0.0.0.0, TRUST_PROXY=1, COOKIE_SECURE=0 (set to 1 after SSL). PM2 is preferred over raw & background commands for long-lived Node.js processes (avoids system blocks). Docker Compose setups for Hermes need extra_hosts: "host.docker.internal:host-gateway" in hermes-agent service to access Ollama on host.

   280|### ⚙️ Penjelasan Setiap Tahapan Pipeline
   281|
   282|1.  **User Input**
   283|    *   Permintaan masuk dari **Telegram** (via Bot API) atau dari **Dashboard** (tombol "Run").
   284|    *   Bisa berupa perintah natural language, slash command (misal `/standup`), atau trigger otomatis (cron job, webhook).
   285|
   286|2.  **API / Ingestion**
   287|    *   Lapisan penerima pesan yang menstandarisasi input sebelum masuk ke Hub.
   288|    *   Di sini pesan mentah diubah menjadi **Task Object** standar (dengan field: `user_id`, `message`, `timestamp`, `channel`).
   289|
   290|3.  **Orchestrator Hub**
   291|    *   Otak utama. Menerima Task Object dan memutuskan:
   292|        *   Apakah ini permintaan untuk **War Room** (diskusi kolaboratif)?
   293|        *   Apakah ini **Auto‑Assign** (routing otomatis ke agen terbaik)?
   294|        *   Apakah memicu **Workflow** yang sudah didefinisikan (misal: file berubah → deploy)?
   295|    *   Hub juga mengelola **Agent Registry** (daftar semua agen yang aktif, status health, capability description).
   296|
   297|4.  **Auto‑Assign (Intent Classification & Routing)**
   298|    *   Model murah (Gemini Flash / Claude Haiku) menganalisis isi permintaan.
   299|    *   Mencocokkan dengan **deskripsi kemampuan** setiap agen di Registry.
   300|    *   Mengembalikan keputusan: agen mana yang paling cocok. Jika tidak ada yang cocok, bisa dikembalikan ke user dengan saran agen baru (seperti fitur "sugesti agen" di dokumen pertama).
   301|
   302|5.  **War Room (Collaborative Discussion)**
   303|    *   Jika user meminta diskusi (misal `/discuss topik X`), Hub menciptakan **sesi percakapan**.
   304|    *   Semua agen dipanggil bergiliran, dengan konteks kumulatif dari respons sebelumnya.
   305|    *   Agen khusus (misal Meta Agent) bisa merangkum hasil akhir.
   306|    *   Perlu penanganan *turn‑taking* dan *state management* agar agen tahu percakapan sebelumnya.
   307|
   308|6.  **Workflow Engine**
   309|    *   Menjalankan alur yang sudah didefinisikan (DAG – Directed Acyclic Graph).
   310|    *   Contoh: `FileTrigger → GameDev.analyze → Builder.review → Infra.deploy`.
   311|    *   Mengelola **dependency** (langkah 2 hanya berjalan jika langkah 1 sukses) dan **error handling** (retry, fallback).
   312|
   313|7.  **Task Dispatcher**
   314|    *   Menerima hasil dari Auto‑Assign / War Room / Workflow Engine.
   315|    *   Mengirimkan tugas ke agen target melalui **Message Queue (Redis)** atau panggilan API langsung.
   316|    *   Bersifat asinkron: tugas masuk ke antrian, agen mengambilnya saat siap.
   317|
   318|8.  **Agent Execution**
   319|    *   Setiap agen (Loyx, GameDev, Builder, Infra, Plaza) adalah proses independen yang memiliki **Agent Adapter** (REST API wrapper).
   320|    *   Adapter menerima tugas, menjalankan *skill* yang diminta, dan melaporkan hasilnya kembali ke Hub.
   321|    *   Agen bisa saling **request skill** dari **Skill Registry** (lihat langkah berikutnya).
   322|
   323|9.  **Skill Registry**
   324|    *   Direktori pusat yang menyimpan definisi semua *skill* (fungsi) yang bisa dipakai.
   325|    *   Bersifat **global** (semua agen bisa akses) atau **lokal** (khusus satu agen).
   326|    *   Saat agen butuh *skill* yang tidak dimilikinya, ia bisa memanggil Registry → Registry meneruskan ke agen yang memiliki *skill* tersebut.
   327|    *   Ini adalah fondasi **modularitas** dan **penghematan biaya**, seperti dijelaskan di PDF 2.
   328|
   329|10. **Shared Memory**
   330|    *   Setiap kali tugas selesai, ringkasan eksekusi (input, output, agen yang terlibat, *timestamp*) ditulis ke memori bersama (bisa SQLite/Obsidian vault).
   331|    *   Memori memiliki beberapa lapisan (penting, biasa, sementara) dan bisa dicari (*searchable*).
   332|    *   Agen lain bisa **mengakses konteks masa lalu** sebelum memulai tugas baru → ini adalah **Hive Mind**.
   333|
   334|11. **Response & Logging**
   335|    *   Hasil akhir dikirim kembali ke user (Telegram/Dashboard).
   336|    *   Semua aktivitas dicatat di **log terpusat** untuk monitoring dan debugging.

Hermes Orchestration - Shared Memory Module
============================================

Provides centralized memory storage for all Hermes agents.
Enables "Hive Mind" - agents can access context from past work.

Database: SQLite
Location: /root/hermes-orchestration/shared-memory/db/memory.db

Author: Hermes Agent
Created: 2026-05-04
"""

import sqlite3
import json
import time
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Any
from pathlib import Path
import threading

# Database path
DB_PATH = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "db" / "memory.db"
DB_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# Thread-local storage for connections
_thread_local = threading.local()


def get_connection():
    """Get thread-local database connection."""
    if not hasattr(_thread_local, 'connection'):
        _thread_local.connection = sqlite3.connect(str(DB_PATH), check_same_thread=False)
        _thread_local.connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    return _thread_local.connection


def init_database():
    """Initialize database schema."""
    conn = get_connection()
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    # Main memory table
    cursor.execute("""
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS memory (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            agent_id TEXT NOT NULL,
            agent_name TEXT NOT NULL,
            task_type TEXT NOT NULL,
            task_description TEXT NOT NULL,
            input_data TEXT,
            output_data TEXT,
            status TEXT NOT NULL,
            priority INTEGER DEFAULT 5,
            tags TEXT,
            created_at REAL NOT NULL,
            updated_at REAL NOT NULL,
            completed_at REAL,
            duration_seconds REAL,
            metadata TEXT
        )
    """)
    
    # Memory relationships (for linked tasks)
    cursor.execute("""
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS memory_relations (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            parent_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
            child_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
            relation_type TEXT NOT NULL,
            created_at REAL NOT NULL,
            FOREIGN KEY (parent_id) REFERENCES memory(id),
            FOREIGN KEY (child_id) REFERENCES memory(id)
        )
    """)
    
    # Agent activity log
    cursor.execute("""
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS agent_activity (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            agent_id TEXT NOT NULL,
            agent_name TEXT NOT NULL,
            activity_type TEXT NOT NULL,
            description TEXT,
            timestamp REAL NOT NULL,
            metadata TEXT
        )
    """)
    
    # Create indexes for performance
    cursor.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_memory_agent ON memory(agent_id)")
    cursor.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_memory_task_type ON memory(task_type)")
    cursor.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_memory_status ON memory(status)")
    cursor.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_memory_created ON memory(created_at)")
    cursor.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_memory_tags ON memory(tags)")
    cursor.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_activity_agent ON agent_activity(agent_id)")
    cursor.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_activity_timestamp ON agent_activity(timestamp)")
    
    conn.commit()
    return True


def write_memory(
    agent_id: str,
    agent_name: str,
    task_type: str,
    task_description: str,
    input_data: Optional[Dict] = None,
    output_data: Optional[Dict] = None,
    status: str = "pending",
    priority: int = 5,
    tags: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    metadata: Optional[Dict] = None
) -> int:
    """
    Write a memory entry.
    
    Args:
        agent_id: Agent identifier (e.g., "loyx-8643")
        agent_name: Human-readable agent name
        task_type: Type of task (e.g., "code_review", "deployment", "analysis")
        task_description: Brief description of the task
        input_data: Input data for the task (dict)
        output_data: Output/result data (dict)
        status: Task status (pending, in_progress, completed, failed)
        priority: Priority level (1-10, higher = more important)
        tags: List of tags for categorization
        metadata: Additional metadata
    
    Returns:
        Memory ID (integer)
    """
    conn = get_connection()
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    now = time.time()
    
    cursor.execute("""
        INSERT INTO memory (
            agent_id, agent_name, task_type, task_description,
            input_data, output_data, status, priority, tags,
            created_at, updated_at, metadata
        ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
    """, (
        agent_id,
        agent_name,
        task_type,
        task_description,
        json.dumps(input_data) if input_data else None,
        json.dumps(output_data) if output_data else None,
        status,
        priority,
        json.dumps(tags) if tags else None,
        now,
        now,
        json.dumps(metadata) if metadata else None
    ))
    
    memory_id = cursor.lastrowid
    conn.commit()
    
    # Log activity
    log_activity(agent_id, agent_name, "memory_write", f"Created memory #{memory_id}: {task_description}")
    
    return memory_id


def update_memory(
    memory_id: int,
    output_data: Optional[Dict] = None,
    status: Optional[str] = None,
    metadata: Optional[Dict] = None
) -> bool:
    """
    Update an existing memory entry.
    
    Args:
        memory_id: Memory ID to update
        output_data: New output data
        status: New status
        metadata: Additional metadata to merge
    
    Returns:
        True if successful
    """
    conn = get_connection()
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    now = time.time()
    
    # Build update query dynamically
    updates = ["updated_at = ?"]
    params = [now]
    
    if output_data is not None:
        updates.append("output_data = ?")
        params.append(json.dumps(output_data))
    
    if status is not None:
        updates.append("status = ?")
        params.append(status)
        
        if status == "completed":
            # Calculate duration
            cursor.execute("SELECT created_at FROM memory WHERE id = ?", (memory_id,))
            row = cursor.fetchone()
            if row:
                duration = now - row[0]
                updates.append("completed_at = ?")
                updates.append("duration_seconds = ?")
                params.extend([now, duration])
    
    if metadata is not None:
        updates.append("metadata = ?")
        params.append(json.dumps(metadata))
    
    params.append(memory_id)
    
    query = f"UPDATE memory SET {', '.join(updates)} WHERE id = ?"
    cursor.execute(query, params)
    conn.commit()
    
    return cursor.rowcount > 0


def read_memory(
    memory_id: Optional[int] = None,
    agent_id: Optional[str] = None,
    task_type: Optional[str] = None,
    status: Optional[str] = None,
    limit: int = 50,
    offset: int = 0
) -> List[Dict]:
    """
    Read memory entries with filters.
    
    Args:
        memory_id: Specific memory ID
        agent_id: Filter by agent
        task_type: Filter by task type
        status: Filter by status
        limit: Maximum results
        offset: Pagination offset
    
    Returns:
        List of memory entries
    """
    conn = get_connection()
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    query = "SELECT * FROM memory WHERE 1=1"
    params = []
    
    if memory_id is not None:
        query += " AND id = ?"
        params.append(memory_id)
    
    if agent_id is not None:
        query += " AND agent_id = ?"
        params.append(agent_id)
    
    if task_type is not None:
        query += " AND task_type = ?"
        params.append(task_type)
    
    if status is not None:
        query += " AND status = ?"
        params.append(status)
    
    query += " ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?"
    params.extend([limit, offset])
    
    cursor.execute(query, params)
    rows = cursor.fetchall()
    
    results = []
    for row in rows:
        entry = dict(row)
        # Parse JSON fields
        if entry['input_data']:
            entry['input_data'] = json.loads(entry['input_data'])
        if entry['output_data']:
            entry['output_data'] = json.loads(entry['output_data'])
        if entry['tags']:
            entry['tags'] = json.loads(entry['tags'])
        if entry['metadata']:
            entry['metadata'] = json.loads(entry['metadata'])
        
        # Format timestamps
        entry['created_at_human'] = datetime.fromtimestamp(entry['created_at']).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
        if entry['completed_at']:
            entry['completed_at_human'] = datetime.fromtimestamp(entry['completed_at']).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
        
        results.append(entry)
    
    return results


def search_memory(
    query: str,
    agent_id: Optional[str] = None,
    limit: int = 20
) -> List[Dict]:
    """
    Search memory by text query.
    
    Args:
        query: Search query (searches in task_description, input_data, output_data)
        agent_id: Optional agent filter
        limit: Maximum results
    
    Returns:
        List of matching memory entries
    """
    conn = get_connection()
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    search_query = """
        SELECT * FROM memory 
        WHERE (
            task_description LIKE ? OR
            input_data LIKE ? OR
            output_data LIKE ?
        )
    """
    params = [f"%{query}%", f"%{query}%", f"%{query}%"]
    
    if agent_id:
        search_query += " AND agent_id = ?"
        params.append(agent_id)
    
    search_query += " ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?"
    params.append(limit)
    
    cursor.execute(search_query, params)
    rows = cursor.fetchall()
    
    results = []
    for row in rows:
        entry = dict(row)
        if entry['input_data']:
            entry['input_data'] = json.loads(entry['input_data'])
        if entry['output_data']:
            entry['output_data'] = json.loads(entry['output_data'])
        if entry['tags']:
            entry['tags'] = json.loads(entry['tags'])
        if entry['metadata']:
            entry['metadata'] = json.loads(entry['metadata'])
        results.append(entry)
    
    return results


def log_activity(
    agent_id: str,
    agent_name: str,
    activity_type: str,
    description: str,
    metadata: Optional[Dict] = None
):
    """Log agent activity."""
    conn = get_connection()
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    cursor.execute("""
        INSERT INTO agent_activity (
            agent_id, agent_name, activity_type, description, timestamp, metadata
        ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
    """, (
        agent_id,
        agent_name,
        activity_type,
        description,
        time.time(),
        json.dumps(metadata) if metadata else None
    ))
    
    conn.commit()


def get_memory_stats() -> Dict:
    """Get memory statistics."""
    conn = get_connection()
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    stats = {}
    
    # Total memories
    cursor.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM memory")
    stats['total_memories'] = cursor.fetchone()[0]
    
    # By status
    cursor.execute("SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM memory GROUP BY status")
    stats['by_status'] = {row[0]: row[1] for row in cursor.fetchall()}
    
    # By agent
    cursor.execute("SELECT agent_name, COUNT(*) FROM memory GROUP BY agent_name")
    stats['by_agent'] = {row[0]: row[1] for row in cursor.fetchall()}
    
    # By task type
    cursor.execute("SELECT task_type, COUNT(*) FROM memory GROUP BY task_type")
    stats['by_task_type'] = {row[0]: row[1] for row in cursor.fetchall()}
    
    # Recent activity
    cursor.execute("""
        SELECT agent_name, activity_type, description, timestamp 
        FROM agent_activity 
        ORDER BY timestamp DESC 
        LIMIT 10
    """)
    stats['recent_activity'] = [
        {
            'agent': row[0],
            'type': row[1],
            'description': row[2],
            'timestamp': datetime.fromtimestamp(row[3]).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
        }
        for row in cursor.fetchall()
    ]
    
    return stats


# Initialize database on module import
init_database()

{"content":"# Shared Memory API Documentation

## Overview

The Shared Memory module provides centralized memory storage for all Hermes agents, enabling a "Hive Mind" where agents can access context from past work.

**Database:** SQLite  
**Location:** `/root/hermes-orchestration/shared-memory/db/memory.db`

## Installation

```python
# Import the module
from memory import (
    write_memory,
    read_memory,
    update_memory,
    search_memory,
    get_memory_stats,
    log_activity
)
```

## Core Functions

### write_memory()

Write a new memory entry.

```python
memory_id = write_memory(
    agent_id="loyx-8643",
    agent_name="Loyx",
    task_type="code_review",
    task_description="Review PR #123",
    input_data={"pr_number": 123, "files": ["game.py"]},
    output_data={"approved": True, "comments": 3},
    status="completed",
    priority=8,
    tags=["code-review", "regrow"],
    metadata={"reviewer": "loyx", "duration": 120}
)
```

**Parameters:**
- `agent_id` (str): Agent identifier (e.g., "loyx-8643")
- `agent_name` (str): Human-readable agent name
- `task_type` (str): Type of task (e.g., "code_review", "deployment", "analysis")
- `task_description` (str): Brief description
- `input_data` (dict, optional): Input data
- `output_data` (dict, optional): Output/result data
- `status` (str): Task status (pending, in_progress, completed, failed)
- `priority` (int): Priority level (1-10, higher = more important)
- `tags` (list, optional): Tags for categorization
- `metadata` (dict, optional): Additional metadata

**Returns:** Memory ID (integer)

### read_memory()

Read memory entries with filters.

```python
# Read specific memory
memories = read_memory(memory_id=1)

# Read by agent
memories = read_memory(agent_id="loyx-8643")

# Read by task type
memories = read_memory(task_type="code_review")

# Read by status
memories = read_memory(status="completed")

# Pagination
memories = read_memory(limit=10, offset=0)
```

**Parameters:**
- `memory_id` (int, optional): Specific memory ID
- `agent_id` (str, optional): Filter by agent
- `task_type` (str, optional): Filter by task type
- `status` (str, optional): Filter by status
- `limit` (int): Maximum results (default: 50)
- `offset` (int): Pagination offset (default: 0)

**Returns:** List of memory entries (dicts)

### update_memory()

Update an existing memory entry.

```python
success = update_memory(
    memory_id=1,
    output_data={"result": "success"},
    status="completed",
    metadata={"notes": "All tests passed"}
)
```

**Parameters:**
- `memory_id` (int): Memory ID to update
- `output_data` (dict, optional): New output data
- `status` (str, optional): New status
- `metadata` (dict, optional): Additional metadata

**Returns:** True if successful

### search_memory()

Search memory by text query.

```python
# Search across all fields
results = search_memory("deployment")

# Search with agent filter
results = search_memory("error", agent_id="infra-9121")

# Limit results
results = search_memory("regrow", limit=10)
```

**Parameters:**
- `query` (str): Search query (searches in task_description, input_data, output_data)
- `agent_id` (str, optional): Filter by agent
- `limit` (int): Maximum results (default: 20)

**Returns:** List of matching memory entries

### get_memory_stats()

Get memory statistics.

```python
stats = get_memory_stats()

print(stats['total_memories'])  # Total count
print(stats['by_status'])       # Count by status
print(stats['by_agent'])        # Count by agent
print(stats['by_task_type'])    # Count by task type
print(stats['recent_activity']) # Recent activity log
```

**Returns:** Dictionary with statistics

### log_activity()

Log agent activity.

```python
log_activity(
    agent_id="loyx-8643",
    agent_name="Loyx",
    activity_type="task_completed",
    description="Completed code review",
    metadata={"task_id": 123}
)
```

## Database Schema

### memory table

| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| id | INTEGER | Primary key |
| agent_id | TEXT | Agent identifier |
| agent_name | TEXT | Human-readable agent name |
| task_type | TEXT | Type of task |
| task_description | TEXT | Brief description |
| input_data | TEXT | JSON input data |
| output_data | TEXT | JSON output data |
| status | TEXT | Task status |
| priority | INTEGER | Priority (1-10) |
| tags | TEXT | JSON array of tags |
| created_at | REAL | Unix timestamp |
| updated_at | REAL | Unix timestamp |
| completed_at | REAL | Unix timestamp |
| duration_seconds | REAL | Task duration |
| metadata | TEXT | JSON metadata |

### agent_activity table

| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| id | INTEGER | Primary key |
| agent_id | TEXT | Agent identifier |
| agent_name | TEXT | Agent name |
| activity_type | TEXT | Activity type |
| description | TEXT | Description |
| timestamp | REAL | Unix timestamp |
| metadata | TEXT | JSON metadata |

## Usage Examples

### Example 1: Agent completes a task

```python
# Agent starts task
memory_id = write_memory(
    agent_id="gamedev-8644",
    agent_name="GameDev",
    task_type="code_analysis",
    task_description="Analyze new game features",
    input_data={"files": ["player.py", "inventory.py"]},
    status="in_progress",
    priority=8
)

# ... agent does work ...

# Agent completes task
update_memory(
    memory_id=memory_id,
    output_data={
        "issues_found": 2,
        "suggestions": 5,
        "complexity_score": 7.5
    },
    status="completed"
)
```

### Example 2: Agent searches past work

```python
# Before starting a task, check if similar work was done
past_work = search_memory("player inventory system")

if past_work:
    print(f"Found {len(past_work)} related past tasks")
    for work in past_work:
        print(f"  - {work['task_description']} by {work['agent_name']}")
        print(f"    Result: {work['output_data']}")
```

### Example 3: Dashboard queries

```python
# Get all pending tasks
pending = read_memory(status="pending")

# Get recent work by specific agent
recent = read_memory(agent_id="builder-9122", limit=10)

# Get high-priority tasks
high_priority = [m for m in read_memory(limit=100) if m['priority'] >= 8]
```

## Best Practices

1. **Always write memory after completing tasks** - This builds the knowledge base
2. **Use descriptive task_description** - Makes searching easier
3. **Tag appropriately** - Use consistent tags for categorization
4. **Search before starting** - Check if similar work was done before
5. **Update status** - Keep status current (pending → in_progress → completed)
6. **Set priority** - Helps identify important work

Hermes Agent Integration Module for Shared Memory

This module provides easy integration between Hermes agents
and the shared memory system.

Usage:
    from agent_memory import AgentMemory
    
    # Initialize for your agent
    memory = AgentMemory(agent_id="loyx-8643", agent_name="Loyx")
    
    # Start a task
    task_id = memory.start_task(
        task_type="code_review",
        description="Review PR #123",
        input_data={"pr": 123}
    )
    
    # Complete the task
    memory.complete_task(
        task_id=task_id,
        output_data={"approved": True}
    )
    
    # Search past work
    past_work = memory.search("code review")
"""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

# Add memory API to path
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent / "api"))

from memory import (
    write_memory,
    read_memory,
    update_memory,
    search_memory,
    get_memory_stats,
    log_activity
)


class AgentMemory:
    """Simplified interface for Hermes agents to use shared memory."""
    
    def __init__(self, agent_id: str, agent_name: str):
        """
        Initialize agent memory interface.
        
        Args:
            agent_id: Agent identifier (e.g., "loyx-8643")
            agent_name: Human-readable name (e.g., "Loyx")
        """
        self.agent_id = agent_id
        self.agent_name = agent_name
        
        # Log agent initialization
        log_activity(
            agent_id=agent_id,
            agent_name=agent_name,
            activity_type="memory_init",
            description=f"Agent {agent_name} connected to shared memory"
        )
    
    def start_task(self, task_type: str, description: str, 
                   input_data: dict = None, priority: int = 5,
                   tags: list = None) -> int:
        """
        Start a new task and record it in memory.
        
        Args:
            task_type: Type of task (e.g., "code_review", "deployment")
            description: Brief description
            input_data: Input data for the task
            priority: Priority level (1-10)
            tags: List of tags
        
        Returns:
            Task ID (memory_id)
        """
        memory_id = write_memory(
            agent_id=self.agent_id,
            agent_name=self.agent_name,
            task_type=task_type,
            task_description=description,
            input_data=input_data,
            status="in_progress",
            priority=priority,
            tags=tags
        )
        
        return memory_id
    
    def complete_task(self, task_id: int, output_data: dict = None,
                      success: bool = True):
        """
        Mark a task as completed.
        
        Args:
            task_id: Task ID from start_task()
            output_data: Result data
            success: Whether task succeeded
        """
        status = "completed" if success else "failed"
        
        update_memory(
            memory_id=task_id,
            output_data=output_data,
            status=status
        )
        
        log_activity(
            agent_id=self.agent_id,
            agent_name=self.agent_name,
            activity_type="task_completed",
            description=f"Completed task #{task_id}",
            metadata={"task_id": task_id, "success": success}
        )
    
    def fail_task(self, task_id: int, error: str):
        """
        Mark a task as failed.
        
        Args:
            task_id: Task ID
            error: Error message
        """
        update_memory(
            memory_id=task_id,
            output_data={"error": error},
            status="failed"
        )
    
    def search(self, query: str, limit: int = 10):
        """
        Search past work.
        
        Args:
            query: Search query
            limit: Max results
        
        Returns:
            List of matching memories
        """
        return search_memory(query, agent_id=self.agent_id, limit=limit)
    
    def search_all_agents(self, query: str, limit: int = 10):
        """
        Search past work across all agents.
        
        Args:
            query: Search query
            limit: Max results
        
        Returns:
            List of matching memories from any agent
        """
        return search_memory(query, limit=limit)
    
    def get_my_recent_work(self, limit: int = 10):
        """
        Get recent work by this agent.
        
        Args:
            limit: Max results
        
        Returns:
            List of recent memories
        """
        return read_memory(agent_id=self.agent_id, limit=limit)
    
    def get_pending_tasks(self):
        """Get all pending tasks for this agent."""
        return read_memory(agent_id=self.agent_id, status="pending")
    
    def get_in_progress_tasks(self):
        """Get all in-progress tasks for this agent."""
        return read_memory(agent_id=self.agent_id, status="in_progress")
    
    def log(self, activity_type: str, description: str, metadata: dict = None):
        """
        Log an activity.
        
        Args:
            activity_type: Type of activity
            description: Description
            metadata: Additional metadata
        """
        log_activity(
            agent_id=self.agent_id,
            agent_name=self.agent_name,
            activity_type=activity_type,
            description=description,
            metadata=metadata
        )
    
    def get_stats(self):
        """Get memory statistics."""
        return get_memory_stats()
    
    def check_similar_work(self, description: str, limit: int = 5):
        """
        Check if similar work was done before.
        
        Args:
            description: Task description to search for
            limit: Max results
        
        Returns:
            List of similar past work
        """
        results = search_memory(description, limit=limit)
        
        if results:
            self.log(
                "memory_search",
                f"Found {len(results)} similar past work for: {description}"
            )
        
        return results


# Convenience function for quick integration
def get_agent_memory(agent_id: str, agent_name: str) -> AgentMemory:
    """
    Quick way to get agent memory interface.
    
    Usage:
        memory = get_agent_memory("loyx-8643", "Loyx")
    """

function.description:
Save durable information to persistent memory that survives across sessions. Memory is injected into future turns, so keep it compact and focused on facts that will still matter later.

WHEN TO SAVE (do this proactively, don't wait to be asked):
- User corrects you or says 'remember this' / 'don't do that again'
- User shares a preference, habit, or personal detail (name, role, timezone, coding style)
- You discover something about the environment (OS, installed tools, project structure)
- You learn a convention, API quirk, or workflow specific to this user's setup
- You identify a stable fact that will be useful again in future sessions

PRIORITY: User preferences and corrections > environment facts > procedural knowledge. The most valuable memory prevents the user from having to repeat themselves.

Do NOT save task progress, session outcomes, completed-work logs, or temporary TODO state to memory; use session_search to recall those from past transcripts.
If you've discovered a new way to do something, solved a problem that could be necessary later, save it as a skill with the skill tool.

TWO TARGETS:
- 'user': who the user is -- name, role, preferences, communication style, pet peeves
- 'memory': your notes -- environment facts, project conventions, tool quirks, lessons learned

ACTIONS: add (new entry), replace (update existing -- old_text identifies it), remove (delete -- old_text identifies it).

SKIP: trivial/obvious info, things easily re-discovered, raw data dumps, and temporary task state.

function.name: skill_manage
function.description:
Manage skills (create, update, delete). Skills are your procedural memory — reusable approaches for recurring task types. New skills go to ~/.hermes/skills/; existing skills can be modified wherever they live.

Actions: create (full SKILL.md + optional category), patch (old_string/new_string — preferred for fixes), edit (full SKILL.md rewrite — major overhauls only), delete, write_file, remove_file.

On delete, pass `absorbed_into=<umbrella>` when you're merging this skill's content into another one, or `absorbed_into=""` when you're pruning it with no forwarding target. This lets the curator tell consolidation from pruning without guessing, so downstream consumers (cron jobs that reference the old skill name, etc.) get updated correctly. The target you name in `absorbed_into` must already exist — create/patch the umbrella first, then delete.

Create when: complex task succeeded (5+ calls), errors overcome, user-corrected approach worked, non-trivial workflow discovered, or user asks you to remember a procedure.
Update when: instructions stale/wrong, OS-specific failures, missing steps or pitfalls found during use. If you used a skill and hit issues not covered by it, patch it immediately.

After difficult/iterative tasks, offer to save as a skill. Skip for simple one-offs. Confirm with user before creating/deleting.

Good skills: trigger conditions, numbered steps with exact commands, pitfalls section, verification steps. Use skill_view() to see format examples.

Pinned skills are off-limits — all write actions refuse with a message pointing the user to `hermes curator unpin <name>`. Don't try to route around this by renaming or recreating.
